intended_object: The standard (normalized) identification Hom(K,L)[s−r] ≅ Hom(K⟦r⟧, L⟦s⟧) in degree n, sending a cochain z of degree n+(s−r) from K to L to the cochain from K⟦r⟧ to L⟦s⟧ with components (−1)^{rn} z^{i+r, j+s}. It is the action on Hom complexes of the DG functor K[r] ↦ K⟦r⟧ from the formal shift closure of cochain complexes (inferred from the docstring and module doc).
explanation: The body composes two maps. The first is `dgHomEquiv`, which is `LinearEquiv.refl`, since in the shift closure a degree-n morphism K[r] ⟶ L[s] is by definition a degree-(n+s−r) morphism K ⟶ L. The second is `cochainShiftLinearEquiv`, built from Mathlib's `Cochain.rightShiftLinearEquiv` and `Cochain.leftShiftLinearEquiv`, then scaled by (−1)^{r(r−1)/2}. The lemma `cochainShiftLinearEquiv_v` proves the components are exactly (r*n).negOnePow • z.v (i+r) (j+s), as the docstring says. The library also proves this map intertwines the shift-closure differential (−1)^{s−r}δ with δ and matches the Koszul-signed composition, so it assembles into a DG functor that is an isomorphism on Hom complexes. This confirms the sign convention is the correct normalized identification. The setting (ℤ-indexed cochain complexes in an R-linear preadditive category) is what the construction needs: integer shifts require ℤ indexing, and R-linearity makes the Hom complexes R-modules. Restricting to the shift closure of cochain complexes is part of what the object is. Mathlib provides only the building blocks (left and right shifts of cochains), not this identification for a DG shift closure.
